questions.q: What does a catalog binding actually control, beyond what Lesson 38 covered?
options: Which specific workspaces attached to a metastore can see and use a particular catalog
Which individual users can query a specific table
How much compute a cluster can use
The physical cloud region a metastore is stored in
questions.explain: A metastore can attach to many workspaces, but a catalog inside it can be bound to just a subset of those workspaces specifically.

questions.q: Why does Databricks recommend one metastore per region instead of one per team?
options: Splitting metastores per team recreates the same per-workspace permission silos Unity Catalog was built to eliminate
Multiple metastores per region are technically impossible to create
A team-specific metastore is always faster to query
There is no real difference between one metastore per region and one per team
questions.explain: Unity Catalog's shared-governance benefit only holds if there's actually one shared metastore to govern — isolation is handled by catalog bindings instead.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what did Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 38 already cover in full?
options: The object hierarchy: metastore, catalog, schema, table/view/volume/function
Row-level and column-level security patterns at scale
Delta Sharing between organizations
The DP-750 certification exam structure
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly builds on that hierarchy rather than re-teaching it, per this course's stated approach.

questions.q: What does this chapter's Lesson 4 (Unity Catalog Volumes) add beyond Lesson 45's original coverage?
options: File-access patterns a single introductory example didn't cover
Nothing — it's an identical repeat of Lesson 45
A replacement for catalogs and schemas entirely
A new way to create clusters
questions.explain: This chapter revisits several Lesson 38-45 topics at production scale rather than repeating the introductory treatment.

questions.q: Can a single metastore be attached to more than one Databricks workspace?
options: Yes — that's exactly the shared-governance model Unity Catalog is designed around
No — each workspace requires its own dedicated metastore
Only if the workspaces are in different cloud regions
Only for read-only access, never for write access
questions.explain: A metastore attached to multiple workspaces means a permission granted once applies everywhere that metastore is attached.
